---
title: Semantic
---

Semantic HTML5 elements should pass through. Feed readers increasingly render
modern HTML structures correctly, so preserving `<details>`, `<figure>`,
`<blockquote cite>`, `<time datetime>`, and friends retains authorial intent.

Padding: this post walks through a handful of semantic elements to prove they
survive the sanitizer. Not every reader will render `<details>` as an
interactive disclosure — some flatten to a block — but even the flat rendering
preserves the content.

## Figure

<figure>
  <img src="https://cdn.example.com/photo.jpg" alt="A photo" />
  <figcaption>Credit: an example photographer</figcaption>
</figure>

## Blockquote with cite

<blockquote cite="https://example.org/source">
  <p>We shape our tools and thereafter our tools shape us.</p>
</blockquote>

## Details / Summary

<details open>
  <summary>Click to expand</summary>
  <p>Hidden content here.</p>
</details>
